stemMd: A shop marks an item up by 50% above its cost, then gives a 20% discount on the marked price. What is its profit as a percentage of cost?
explanationMd: Let cost be c. Marked price is 1.5c and discounted selling price is 0.8 × 1.5c = 1.2c. Profit is 0.2c, or 20% of cost. Track the base of each percentage separately.

distractorRationale.d: This subtracts percentages with different bases.
distractorRationale.a: This does not use the correct product of price factors.
distractorRationale.c: Profit is 0.2 times cost and sales are 1.2 times cost; even profit as a fraction of sales would be 16⅔%, not 25%.
